title: Review: The box office report
explanation: **Level 3 review!** A film studio has 18 movies from the first half of the year in `box_office`: genre, release month, rating, gross and budget (in $ millions). Answer the studio head's questions with grouped summaries. There's nothing new here, just everything from Level 3.

tasks.prompt: For each genre, count the movies (movies) and add up the gross (total_gross), biggest total first.
hints: group_by, summarize with 2 summaries, then arrange(desc()).
result <- box_office |> group_by(genre) |> summarize(movies = n(), total_gross = sum(gross)) |> arrange(desc(total_gross))
tasks.answer: result <- box_office |> group_by(genre) |> summarize(movies = n(), total_gross = sum(gross)) |> arrange(desc(total_gross))

tasks.prompt: Add a profit column (gross − budget), then find the average profit per rating, rounded to 1 decimal, in avg_profit.
hints: mutate first, then group_by and summarize.
result <- box_office |> mutate(profit = gross - budget) |> group_by(rating) |> summarize(avg_profit = round(mean(profit), 1))
tasks.answer: result <- box_office |> mutate(profit = gross - budget) |> group_by(rating) |> summarize(avg_profit = round(mean(profit), 1))

tasks.prompt: Find the single best month by total gross: one row with month and total_gross.
hints: Summarise by month, then keep the top 1 (slice_max, or arrange + head).
result <- box_office |> group_by(month) |> summarize(total_gross = sum(gross)) |> slice_max(total_gross, n = 1)
tasks.answer: result <- box_office |> group_by(month) |> summarize(total_gross = sum(gross)) |> slice_max(total_gross, n = 1)

tasks.prompt: Last one: for genres with at least 3 movies, find the average gross (avg_gross, rounded to 1 decimal), highest first. Keep the movies column too.
hints: summarize, then filter on movies, then arrange.
result <- box_office |> group_by(genre) |> summarize(movies = n(), avg_gross = round(mean(gross), 1)) |> filter(movies >= 3) |> arrange(desc(avg_gross))
tasks.answer: result <- box_office |> group_by(genre) |> summarize(movies = n(), avg_gross = round(mean(gross), 1)) |> filter(movies >= 3) |> arrange(desc(avg_gross))

recap: Level 3 done! You can summarise whole tables or each group, count quickly, handle NAs, filter groups after summarising, and use across() for many columns. Next up: cleaning messy data.
